newsitem.title: FRANCE: French election starts, Chirac gambles presidency.
newsitem.headline: French election starts, Chirac gambles presidency.

text.p: Voting began in France on Sunday for the first round of a parliamentary election in which President Jacques Chirac is gambling on winning a renewed centre-right majority.

Polling stations opened at 8 a.m. (0600 GMT) in mainland France and close at 8 p.m. (1800 GMT). France's 39 million voters are to choose 577 National Assembly deputies, with a second run-off round on June 1.

Weather was sunny across much of France but with some rain forecast in the south. The vote follows a lacklustre campaign dominated by clashes over personalities, record unemployment, weak economic growth and European policies.

Opinion polls before a publication blackout a week ago showed the centre-right was likely to win a reduced majority. Conservative Chirac, whose seven-year term runs until 2002, has said France needs a "new elan", partly to enter a single European currency from a position of strength.

He is risking his presidency with the vote -- if French citizens elect the opposition Socialists he will be forced into an uneasy "cohabitation" with a government led by a prime minister Lionel Jospin.
First results, and predictions of the likely outcome of run-off races next Sunday, are due immediately after the close of polling.
